findings.breaking_input: Run the fixture on a Windows checkout with core.autocrlf=true. Every contract file then has CRLF line endings.
findings.why: The fixture splits on "\n", so each line keeps a trailing "\r". The regex ends in `,$`, which does not match a line ending "\r". duplicateOneKey returns null, the vacuous-pass guard fires, and the test goes red on exactly the Windows leg. Defect pattern: autocrlf / CRLF handling.
findings.fix: Split on /\r?\n/ and re-join with the file's own EOL, or let the regex tolerate \r with `,\r?$`.
findings.twin_of: `--chart --check` compared raw bytes, so an autocrlf checkout read as a hand edit

findings.breaking_input: Any run. mkdtempSync creates a temp dir holding three full copies of .claude/scripts, docs, initiatives/face and more. Nothing ever removes it, and a SIGTERM from a CI cancel leaves it behind too.
findings.why: There is no rmSync, no try/finally and no signal handler, so every run leaks three trees. Docs and scripts can be tens of MB.
findings.fix: Wrap the loop in try/finally with rmSync(tmp, {recursive:true, force:true}), open the try right after mkdtemp, and add a SIGTERM/SIGINT handler.
findings.twin_of: The self-test cleaned its scratch tree on SIGINT only; a CI cancel sends SIGTERM

findings.breaking_input: cpSync of a directory fails with EACCES, ENAMETOOLONG (long Windows temp path) or EMFILE, for example for .claude/scripts.
findings.why: The bare `catch { /* absent on this tree */ }` swallows every copy error, so the scratch tree is silently incomplete. The gates then fail for an unrelated reason such as a missing parser import. `r.status !== 0` passes, and the name check (`out.includes(file)` plus /duplicate/i) can be satisfied by unrelated text that mentions the file or the word "duplicate". The mutant arms pass without ever exercising the new check.
findings.fix: Only skip when !existsSync(src). Rethrow any other error. Add a control run of both gates on the unmutated scratch copy, so the copy is proven good before the mutants run.
findings.twin_of: `treeScripts` swallowed every read error, so EACCES or EIO shrank the script inventory in silence

findings.breaking_input: Many FAIL lines are printed, then the final "RAN dup-keys N checks, M failed" line, then process.exit(failed ? 1 : 0). The bats `run` reads stdout through a pipe.
findings.why: process.exit straight after a burst of console.log can truncate piped stdout on Windows. The "RAN dup-keys " assertion in the bats file would then report that the fixture never ran.
findings.fix: Set process.exitCode and let the process drain, instead of calling process.exit.
findings.twin_of: The test probe exited with `process.exit(1)` right after a burst of output

findings.breaking_input: A gate child hits its spawnSync timeout. status is null and r.error is ETIMEDOUT.
findings.why: `r.status !== 0` is true for null, so a hung gate counts as 'failed on the duplicate'. Only the output-name check backs it up, and a truncated stdout can still contain the file name. The worst-case wall time is about 2×(120s+300s) for the controls plus 6 mutant runs, with no stated ceiling against the bats or job timeout.
findings.fix: Require typeof r.status === 'number' and !r.error before accepting a non-zero exit. Budget the total and state it.
findings.twin_of: The self-test spawned each arm with no timeout, so one hung child held the whole suite until the CI job limit

findings.breaking_input: A contract file saved by Notepad with a UTF-8 BOM and containing a duplicate key.
findings.why: strictJson hands the BOM-prefixed text to assertNoDuplicateKeys and then to JSON.parse. If the scanner is not BOM-aware, the first key is misread, which is the known BOM pattern. A duplicate of the first key could also slip past, and the error would surface as a parse error rather than a duplicate error.
findings.fix: Strip a leading U+FEFF once in strictJson, before both the scan and the parse.
findings.twin_of: A UTF-8 BOM (Notepad) became part of the first key and failed a card for an invisible byte

findings.breaking_input: Edit strictJson in one of the two files and not the other.
findings.why: The identical strictJson helper is pasted into face-coverage.mjs and face-sections.mjs, so it can drift. Its basename derivation `p.split(/[\\/]/).pop()` is also hand-restated in both. A fix applied in one file leaves the other open, which is the twin-fix recurrence this lane keeps hitting.
findings.fix: Export one `readJsonStrict(path)` from json-strict.mjs and import it in both gates.
findings.twin_of: The emitter's ": " guard copied one misread by hand and could miss a sibling
